results.implication: PF > 1.3 on a reverse-split / dilution wreck suggests fake fills, missing borrow cost, or a bad split adjustment - a HARNESS bug, not an edge.
the same long strategy cannot genuinely profit on a 3x bull ETF and its 3x bear twin over the same window; suspect signal logic or data mislabeling.
win rate > 85% on 20+ trades with a stop on every trade suggests the stop is unreachable or exits resolve in the strategy favor.
a strategy producing zero trades on more than 60% of tickers has a broken trigger condition, not a selective one.
near-identical trade counts across many tickers means these are one idea counted twice; effective test count and any breadth claim are overstated.
large 5m-vs-15m divergence on the same ticker and exit suggests a resampling or timestamp-alignment bug.
mixed gate versions mean some verdicts were produced under different rules; the graveyard cannot be read as one dataset.
mixed cost-model versions mean the same trade costs different amounts in different rows; pooled edges and per-trade means are meaningless across them.

multiple_comparisons.note: With 509080 tests, chance alone is expected to produce a best result around 5.1 sigma. A single impressive row is the base rate, not evidence. Judge must correct on hypotheses GENERATED, and use effective test count (correlated tickers/timeframes are not independent), not raw row count.

graveyard_summary.reading_guide: raw_pass_rows counts (strategy, ticker, timeframe, exit_config) rows. One strategy that works on one ticker across 9 exit configs produces 9 rows and ONE finding. Always cite distinct_findings.
